policy_title: Create a National Care Service and Reform Social Care
stated: Labour will undertake a programme of reform to create a National Care Service, underpinned by national standards and locally delivered with a 'home first' principle. New standards will ensure high-quality care and provider responsibility. Local partnerships between the NHS and social care will improve hospital discharge. A Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care will set fair pay, terms, conditions, and training standards. The party commits to guaranteeing rights for residential care residents to see families and will explore long-term reforms for an ageing population and integration with the NHS.

source.quote: Labour will undertake a programme of reform to create a National Care Service, underpinned by national standards, delivering consistency of care across the country. Services will be locally delivered, with a principle of ‘home first’ that supports people to live independently for as long as possible. Our new standards will ensure high-quality care and ongoing sustainability, and ensure providers behave responsibly. Labour will develop local partnership working between the NHS and social care on hospital discharge. We will enhance partnership working across employers, workers, trade unions and government and establish a Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care. This sector collective agreement will set fair pay, terms and conditions, along with training standards. Labour will consult widely on the design of this agreement, before beginning the process and learn from countries where they operate successfully. Labour is committed to ensuring families have the support they need. We will guarantee the rights of those in residential care to be able to see their families. Alongside these changes, we will build consensus for the longerterm reform needed to create a sustainable National Care Service. We will explore how we best manage and support an ageing population; how integration with the NHS can be secured; how to best support working age disabled adults; and how to move to a more preventative system.

bearing_set.reason: Directly restructures social care access, quality, and funding for older and disabled people — core to dignified later-life support.
A Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care would set pay, terms, conditions, and training standards for a large, predominantly low-paid workforce.
Local NHS–social care partnerships targeting hospital discharge directly affect NHS capacity and waiting pressures.
Policy explicitly 'guarantees rights' for residential care residents to see family — this creates a legal right for a defined group, squarely within O9's civil-liberties/equal-treatment scope.

Raising pay floors in a sector dominated by low-paid, predominantly female and minority-ethnic workers narrows the income gap; national care standards also reduce wealth-based inequality in care access.
Creating a National Care Service is a large spending commitment; the policy does not specify a funding mechanism, so there is a plausible and concrete fiscal pressure on debt-path sustainability.

membership_note: The policy has five clear bearings: its direct target (O8), a concrete NHS spillover (O3), a significant workforce/pay intervention (O4), a distributional effect on low earners (O14), and an uncosted spending commitment (O12).
